div.l: Ne thouh I speke here wordys ꝓpropyrly
For this ye knowen / as wel as I .
Who so shal tellyn / a tale aftir a man
He mote reherce / as nyh as he can
Euerych word / if it be in his charge
Al speke he / nevyr so rudly ne large
Or ellys he mot lellyn / his tale vntrue
Or feynyn thyngis / or fynden wordis newe
He may not spare / al thouh he wer his brothir
He mote as wel seyn / o word as a nothir
Cryst spake him self / ryht brood in holy wryt
And wel ye wetyn / no velanye is it
Eeke plato seyth / who so can him rede
The wordys / mot be cosyn to the dede
And also I pray you / for yf it me
Al haue I set folk / nat in her degree
Here in this tale / as they shuld stond
My wyt is short / ye may wel vndirstond
GReet cheer maade / our ost vs euerychoıı̄un
And to the souper / set he vs a noon
He served vs wᵗith. vytayle / at the best
Strong was the wyn / and wel to drynke vs liste
A semely man / our hoost w was wᵗith all
For to haue ben / a marchal in a hall
A large man he was / wᵗith eyen stepe
A fairer burgeys / is ther noon in chepe
Bold of his speche / was and wel I tawht
And of manhood / him lacked ryht nowht
Eeek therto he was / ryht a mery man
And aftir souper / pleyen he bi gan
And spake of mirth / a mong other thynges
What that we hadde maad / oure rekenynges
And said thus / nowe lordynges trewly
